agree.reason: The candid tone and the plain note that the ratings came from convention players would earn some trust from a wary backer, but this reader also wants a delivery date, a refund promise and a budget, and none of them appear, so they would likely hold back.

honest.reason: It refuses to call the game a hit and is open about where the 23 ratings came from, but it adds a detail nobody supplied ('each session showed me something to fix') and says the goal 'pays for the print run' without showing that $17,400 plus shipping plus about 10% in fees fits inside $28,000.

works_the_facts.reason: The only figure it works out is 572 backers; it never sets that against the 1,240 sign-ups (about a 46% conversion needed), never gives the cost per copy ($11.60 to print plus $9 to ship), and never shows how the budget adds up once fees are taken.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative (no print run if the goal is missed, and the game stays on the creator's table) correctly but only in passing, and it does not compare the cost of a pledge with that outcome.

qualification.reason: The only commitment is updates every two weeks, and that cadence is still a bracketed placeholder; there is no November delivery date and no full refund if delivery runs more than three months late, so the reader has nothing to check against a date and a consequence.

objections.reason: It names the first-time-creator worry directly, but answers it with playtest history rather than the things that actually lower risk (delivery date, refund guarantee, signed factory quote, finished rules, the reviewer video in launch week), all of which the user could have supplied.

fit.reason: It is a pitch of about 500 words with sensible sections, but it ships with unfilled placeholders for the game name, the creator's name and the update schedule.
